items.name: Capsule Dream
items.description: 🚗 A wild dream of capsule towers.

items.name: Base Blob
items.description: 🏩 A blobby two storey office building with an entrance hall and access to the staircases and elevators of the round cores on the groundfloor. It has a setback and a colonade towards the street. On the second floor are the office rooms.

items.name: Base
items.description: 🏠 A polygonal two storey office building with an entrance hall and access to the staircases and elevators of the rectangular cores on the groundfloor. It has a setback and a colonade towards the street. On the second floor are the office rooms.

items.name: Bridge
items.description: 🏢 A bridge with two segments an addition on the west along the main path.

items.name: Capital
items.description: 🏗 A roof that has the skin of a cut extruded cuboid.

items.name: Cylindric Capital
items.description: 🏥 A roof that has the skin of a cut extruded cylinder.

items.name: Single Storey Tambour
items.description:
🪤 An efficient one storey tambour for a rectangular shaft core with an elevator in the center, the main platform on the north, and on the other corners sides platforms with two doors. There is a stair between 
every platform. The doors are spiraling around.

items.name: Slanted
items.description: 🚕 A sloped variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules have balconies and the towers are graduated in opposing directions. Each tower has a direction and every floor is stepped in this direction.

items.name: Twisted
items.description: 🚙 A twisted variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules are trapezoids and towers are round with the floors twisting in one direction.

items.name: Dancing
items.description: 🚓 The expolsion axonometry of a futuristic variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where two towers are dancing with each other. The capsules are ellipsoids around a round shaft and a blob base.

items.name: Flat
items.description: 🚑 The digital shadow of the former Nakagin Capsule Tower which was a mixed-use residential and office tower designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa and located in Shimbashi, Tokyo, Japan. Completed in 1972, the building was a rare remaining example of Japanese Metabolism, an architectural movement emblematic of Japan's postwar cultural resurgence.
